fixes.fix: Explained "Errors that can occur may be mechanical (such as card transport mechanisms; keypads; hard "
fixes.text: VERDICT: The missing word is communications. WHY: Banking systems rely on data transmission between branches, ATMs, and servers. Failures in this data flow are distinct from hardware or software bugs. TRAPS: Do not confuse this with 'communication' (singular) or 'connectivity'. The option 'communicat' is a truncated form of the correct noun. HOOK: Think of the bank as a body: mechanical is the skeleton, software is the brain, and communications are the nerves. Exam-day trap: If you see 'network'

fixes.page: archive (Banking & Financial System / Banking & Financial System)
fixes.fix: Explained "According to the ATM Industry Association (ATMIA), as of 2015, there were close to _____ A"
fixes.text: VERDICT: The correct figure is 3.5 million. WHY: ATMIA data from 2015 pegged global ATM infrastructure at this scale, reflecting peak physical cash access before digital shifts. TRAPS: Do not confuse this with India's domestic count (approx. 200,000) or older 2010 estimates. HOOK: Remember 3.5 million as the 'digital cash ceiling' of 2015; examiners love testing specific global banking stats against regional data.

fixes.page: archive (Banking & Financial System / Banking & Financial System)
fixes.fix: Explained "In _____, Armenian-American inventor Luther Simjian invented an automated deposit machine "
fixes.text: 1) VERDICT: 1960. 2) WHY: Luther Simjian filed his US patent for an automated deposit machine on 30 June 1960. It accepted coins, cash, and cheques but lacked cash dispensing. 3) TRAPS: Do not confuse the filing year (1960) with the grant year (1963). Also, note it was a deposit-only device, not a full ATM. 4) HOOK: Remember 'Simjian 1960' as the first step in ATM evolution. Exam trap: Questions often mix up filing vs. grant dates; always prioritize the filing year for invention timelines.
